URL: https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/reform-would-win-fewer-seats-than-labour-and-tories-poll-suggests-trw6rrbb9
The Times — published Thursday 24 September 2026, 05:00 BST — Oliver Wright, Policy Editor

HEADLINE: Reform would win fewer seats than Labour and Tories, poll suggests
SUBHEAD: In a dramatic reversal of last year's survey, YouGov projects a hung parliament, with Labour on top and Nigel Farage's party squeezed by the rise of Restore

FACTS:
- Reform UK would win fewer seats than both Labour and the Conservatives if a general election were held today.
- YouGov MRP projection (for The Times and Sky News): Labour 241 seats; Conservatives 130; Reform UK 123; Liberal Democrats 71; SNP 48*; Plaid Cymru 15; Greens 9. (*chart shows SNP 48; body text says "The SNP would take 40 seats, up from the eight it holds currently" — figures differ between chart and copy; treat SNP with caution.)
- 2025 MRP comparison (September last year): Reform 311 seats — just shy of an overall majority — Labour 144, Conservatives 45.
- Labour currently holds 403 seats; the projection implies a loss of 162.
- Labour would have to rely on support from both the Lib Dems (71) and the Greens (9), or one of the nationalist parties, to command a Commons majority.
- Even if Reform and the Tories agreed a pact, they would not have enough seats to form a majority coalition.
- Vote shares: Reform down from 27% in September last year to 22%; Conservatives up from 17% to 21%; Labour up three points to 24%.
- Restore Britain, the rival right-wing party led by former Reform MP Rupert Lowe, is taking more than three percentage points from Reform's vote and costing it seats in marginal constituencies.
- If replicated, both Robert Jenrick and Suella Braverman — who deserted the Tories to join Farage — would lose their seats to their old party.
- "The only high-profile Labour casualty under the new poll is the health secretary Yvette Cooper, who would lose her seat to Reform."
- Plaid Cymru would take 15 Welsh seats, compared with the four it currently holds. The Greens, despite polling 12%, would win only nine seats, up from five.
- Total sample 14,000 respondents; fieldwork 23 August to 18 September 2026.
- At the last election, YouGov's final MRP called 92% of all seats correctly; it slightly overestimated Reform's seats and underestimated the Tories'.
- Separate YouGov research: more than 40% of Labour and Lib Dem voters would tactically vote Conservative to stop Reform winning in their seat; 26% of Greens said the same; about 15% of Tory voters would back Labour to stop Reform.

QUOTE — PATRICK ENGLISH, head of elections at YouGov: "YouGov's latest projections put Labour clearly ahead of both Reform and the Conservatives in terms of seats, while being only a fraction ahead of each on vote share. While Labour alone remain well short of a majority, there are a wide range of possible 'coalition of the left' options open to them to build a majority in a way where there just simply isn't for Reform and the Conservatives on the right. While the British political left is more fragmented than the right in terms of the number of different parties, their collective vote share is bigger and translates efficiently into seat wins."

Context: Badenoch heads into her second Conservative conference as party leader. Reform has fallen back following the emergence of Restore Britain and "a series of financial scandals".
